newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka Vanik to seek listing of unit.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka Vanik to seek listing of unit.

text.p: Sri Lanka's investment bank Vanik Inc Ltd said on Friday it would list its subsidiary LB Finance Ltd through a flotation on the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE).
Vanik told the CSE in a statement it was slashing its holding in LB Finance, a finance company, to 55 percent from 89 percent by making an offer for the sale of 34 percent.
The offer price would be fixed after discussions with the underwriters, Vanik said.
"We want to make an application for a listing and take the company public for two reasons," Justin Meegoda, CEO and President of Vanik, told Reuters.
"The first is, you do not need nearly 90 percent to control a company. We also want our shareholders to reap the rich rewards due to them from Vanik's restructuring of LB finance."
Vanik took over the ailing finance comapny in 1994 when it had a deposit base of just over 300 million rupees, he said.
"By the six months ended June 1997, we had improved the health of the company which resulted in the deposit base rising to over one billion rupees," Meegoda said.
Vanik said on Thursday it was negotiating with Global Equity Corp to buy the Canadian firm's 50 percent holding of Forbes Ceylon Ltd's issued capital of 240 million shares.
